domain: THE LOOP — canonical continuous self-improving development process
summary: The prior audit's headline conclusion survives: there is a well-written canon (docs/DEVELOPMENT_PROCESS.md v1.1.0), a genuinely strong mechanical-gate substrate (125 gates in `ci:gates`, enforced in GitHub Actions ci.yml AND a pre-push marker), 49 live Vercel crons, and NO autonomous scheduler for the five domain loops. But the prior audit was wrong on two material points and under-credited a third. (1) It claimed "no code path selects Haiku for anything" — false; lib/marketing-brain/audit-classifier.ts:45 and inbox-parser.ts:26 hardcode claude-haiku-4-5, app/actions/crm-inbox.ts:448 uses claude-opus-4-8, both on reachable paths, so per-task model tiering DOES exist in code, just uncentralized and ungated. (2) It described the adversarial-audit capability from SKILL.md prose; the real implementation is stronger — lib/cma/audit.ts is production code with a deterministic verdict function, unit tests, a bounded self-repair re-audit at lib/cma/build.ts:230/269, shared by lib/bpo/build.ts, reachable via the registered /api/cron/cma-build-worker cron. (3) Its "loops have gone dark" framing is misleading: 550 commits landed in the last 14 days, so development is continuous — what is dark is the loops' *state ledgers and named protocols*, not the work. The genuinely damning findings stand and get harder: `site_improvement_ledger` and `process_escape_ledger` have zero code readers/writers anywhere; there is no heartbeat table so a stale loop is indistinguishable from a waiting one; `/api/cron/optimization-loop` is real code that is not in vercel.json; and `out/audits/` has never existed on disk.

items.requirement: A single canonical process document defining the development cycle, mechanically protected from drift
items.evidence: docs/DEVELOPMENT_PROCESS.md (143 lines) — version header line 3 (`**Version: 1.1.0**`), the 10-step cycle lines 13-24, the five-loop topology table lines 30-40, preflight contract lines 47-56, live-env rules lines 58-63, escape protocol line 67, approval model lines 69-73, ledgers lines 75-79, registered-plan table lines 81+. I READ scripts/check-process-canon.mjs in full: it enforces three things — (a) pointer presence in CLAUDE.md, marketing_brain_skills/producers/TEMPLATE.md, lib/marketing-brain/producer-output-class.ts; (b) `THE LOOP vX.Y.Z` in each pointer equals the doc's version header; (c) every docs/plans/*.md basename appears in the canon (rogue-plan check). `ci:process-canon` = `node scripts/check-process-canon.mjs` and is present in the `ci:gates` chain (verified programmatically against package.json).
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor's line citations were approximate and it omitted G44's third and most useful check — the rogue-plan registry.] Verdict unchanged: G44 enforces citation and plan-registration, never execution. Nothing checks that steps 7-9 (measure, learn, lock) ran for any shipped change. The doc's own topology table names `out/audits/` as the immune-system ledger and that directory has never existed (confirmed `ls: out/audits: No such file or directory` while out/ itself holds 40+ other subdirs).
items.why_it_matters: The canon is real and is the best artifact in the domain, but it documents a 10-step cycle of which steps 1-6 happen in sessions and steps 7-9 happen nowhere. G44 makes the doc look enforced.

items.requirement: Domain loops that run continuously and improve their surface without stopping
items.evidence: All five loop skills exist on disk: .claude/skills/{growth-loop,crm-e2e,tc-builder,experience-rollout}/SKILL.md plus facebook-seller-growth. One has a REAL executable probe layer, not just prose: scripts/crm-e2e-verify.mjs (394 lines, writes tmp/crm-e2e-latest.json:394). Staleness re-verified directly on disk, not from docs: tmp/crm-e2e-latest.json mtime Jul 8 19:52 and its own `ranAt` field = 2026-07-09T02:52:00Z — 13 days stale today (2026-07-21), all 34 checks PASS at that snapshot; .auto-memory/fb-ads-loop-state.json mtime Jun 10 18:49 — 41 days stale. tc-builder/SKILL.md:281 `## PAUSED — Matt directive 2026-06-11 (~13:00)` confirmed by direct grep. docs/EXPERIENCE_SYSTEM.md rollout table: families 5-10 all `Pending`, family 2 `LOCKED v7 CINEMATIC` with production still on HomepageHeroV3, families 3-4 `Awaiting review` since 2026-06-10.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor framed this as 'the loops silently go dark for weeks,' implying development stopped. It did not — `git log --since=2026-07-07` returns 550 commits, including a large `refactor(audit): #N` remediation series and `fix(prospecting): adversarial-audit hardening`. What is stale is the loops' STATE LEDGERS and their named protocols, not the engineering.] Sharper finding: work is being done outside the loop protocols, so the ledgers the canon designates as each loop's source of truth (tmp/crm-e2e-latest.json, fb-ads-loop-state.json, EXPERIENCE_SYSTEM.md §Rollout status) no longer describe reality. Additionally scripts/crm-e2e-verify.mjs — the one loop probe that is actual runnable code — is wired into NOTHING: grep across package.json, .github/workflows/, and vercel.json returns zero references. It only runs when a human types the command.
items.why_it_matters: Worse than the auditor said in one way and better in another: the org is shipping constantly, but the process that is supposed to prioritize and measure that shipping is bypassed, so the loop's ledgers are actively misleading rather than merely idle.

items.requirement: An autonomous scheduler that keeps the domain loops firing without a human opening a session
items.evidence: [VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY] I called mcp__scheduled-tasks__list_scheduled_tasks myself. Exactly 3 tasks: `grade-seo-ledger-2026-07-08` (one-time, fired 2026-07-08T16:00Z, now `enabled: false`), `fb-verification-watch` (cron `0 9 * * *`, enabled, last run 2026-07-21T13:45Z — Meta business-verification polling only), `ryan-realty-morning-briefing` (cron `0 7 * * 1-5`, enabled, last run 2026-07-21T14:09Z — read-only briefing). None invokes growth-loop, crm-e2e, tc-builder, or experience-rollout. I also read all 49 vercel.json cron paths: every one is a deterministic API route; none shells out to a Claude session or loads a loop SKILL.md.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] No bridge exists between a typed slash-command and a durable cadence. The mechanism is proven to work (two enabled tasks fired within the last hour) and was simply never pointed at the loops. Note the morning-briefing task's description explicitly claims it reports 'Experience Rollout state' — a read-only status report on a loop nobody is firing, which is why the stall was visible daily for 6 weeks and still not fixed.
items.why_it_matters: Single biggest concrete gap vs the stated goal. Four new scheduled-task entries is a small, directly buildable fix.

items.requirement: Measurement stamping + a learning mechanism that feeds prioritization confidence (canon steps 7-9)
items.evidence: [VERIFIED with a stricter grep than the auditor ran — I grepped ALL file types, not just code extensions.] `site_improvement_ledger` / `process_escape_ledger` appear in exactly 7 files repo-wide: supabase/migrations/20260609230000_loop_ledgers_and_site_signal.sql (the creating migration), docs/DEVELOPMENT_PROCESS.md (lines 21-23, 67, 76-78), docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT.md, .claude/skills/growth-loop/SKILL.md, .auto-memory/memory_experience_system_2026-06-09.md, docs/plans/ultracode-site-consistency-kickoff.md, data/growth/content-moat-backlog.md. ZERO hits in lib/, app/, scripts/, or any .ts/.tsx/.mjs file. No DAL function, no server action, no cron. docs/DEVELOPMENT_PROCESS.md line 21 makes the ledger the `confidence` term in the prioritization formula `score = reach x gap-to-benchmark x confidence / effort`.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor said the ledger has never been exercised at all. Not quite — the scheduled task `grade-seo-ledger-2026-07-08` exists specifically to 'write actual_delta + verdict to site_improvement_ledger' and DID fire once (lastRunAt 2026-07-08T16:00:37Z) before disabling itself. So there is exactly one realized, one-time, human-scheduled agent write path.] The correction makes it worse, not better: the only time step 8 ever executed, it required a bespoke one-off scheduled task, which then turned itself off. The prioritization formula in the canon has a `confidence` input with no production data source, so every cycle re-guesses.
items.why_it_matters: The learning half of the cycle is unimplemented. Nothing gets smarter; the canon asserts a value function it cannot compute.

items.requirement: An adversarial audit / refutation step applied to loop output before it ships
items.evidence: [CORRECTED — the auditor cited SKILL.md prose; the real implementation is materially stronger and I read it.] lib/cma/audit.ts is production TypeScript: header lines 1-17 state builder and auditor share no prompt and that the audit runs on EVERY build; it exports `auditCma` and `computeAuditVerdict` with a typed severity/category/verdict model (lines 28-40). Deterministic verdict logic is unit-tested in lib/cma/audit.test.ts (critical+data-integrity => 'fail', major+price-opinion => 'pass', etc.). Called at lib/cma/build.ts:230, and — the part the auditor missed entirely — lib/cma/build.ts:246-270 implements BOUNDED SELF-REPAIR: on a non-pass verdict it drops the specific comps the auditor flagged, re-prices, and RE-AUDITS once at line 269, never below MIN_COMPS, never more than one round, with both rounds recorded. Shared by lib/bpo/build.ts:32. Reachable in production: lib/cma/worker.ts is driven by /api/cron/cma-build-worker, registered in vercel.json (`14,44 * * * *`). Recent commit ec73497f 'fix(prospecting): adversarial-audit hardening across the send path' shows the pattern spreading to a second surface.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor undersold this as prose in a SKILL.md and missed the self-repair re-audit loop and the BPO reuse.] The verdict still stands though: it is CMA/BPO-shaped, not generic. `auditCma` takes CmaSubject/CmaAdjustedComp/CmaPricing/CmaMarketContext — its signature is welded to valuation, so no other loop can call it without a rewrite. None of growth-loop, crm-e2e, tc-builder, or experience-rollout has any refutation step; their verify step is tsc/tests/ci:gates/browser-render, which catches breakage, not wrongness.
items.why_it_matters: The best template for the missing loop-wide primitive already exists as working, tested, cron-reachable code with a self-repair round. Extracting a domain-agnostic version is a port, not an invention.

items.requirement: Efficient, codified model routing — cheaper models for smaller work, strongest model for complex work
items.evidence: [CORRECTED — the auditor's core factual claim here is FALSE.] It wrote: 'No file in the repo implements a complexity classifier, a task-size heuristic, or any code path that selects Haiku for anything.' Direct grep refutes this: lib/marketing-brain/audit-classifier.ts:45 `const HAIKU_MODEL = 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'` (its own header line 9 documents the cost rationale, '~$0.0008/post for bulk tagging'); lib/marketing-brain/inbox-parser.ts:26 same constant; app/actions/crm-inbox.ts:448 `model: 'claude-opus-4-8'` for SMS drafting. Both Haiku paths are REACHABLE: audit-classifier is imported by lib/marketing-brain/audit-run.ts:25 (`classifyAuditCorpus`), which backs app/api/cron/marketing-audit-run/route.ts:27 (`runAudit`), registered in vercel.json (`0 11 * * 2`); inbox-parser is imported by lib/marketing-brain/inbox-poll.ts:38 and inbox-dispatcher.ts:20. The auditor's other citations check out: app/api/cron/producer-runtime/route.ts:44 `const MODEL = 'claude-sonnet-4-5'` used at lines 232/246/284/308/327/341; lib/cma/audit.ts:24 independently hardcodes the same Sonnet id.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: routing by task tier DOES exist in code — bulk classification on Haiku, producer execution and adversarial audit on Sonnet, broker SMS drafting on Opus. The auditor asserted the opposite.] The real gap is different and narrower: routing is a hardcoded per-call-site constant repeated in at least 5 files with no shared module, no classifier, no cost ceiling tied to the choice, and no gate preventing a new call site from defaulting to the most expensive model. There is also a model-id inconsistency worth flagging: crm-inbox.ts pins `claude-opus-4-8` while everything else pins dated Sonnet/Hauku ids, so upgrades require hand-editing N files.
items.why_it_matters: Cheaper than the auditor implied — the discipline is already being applied by hand. What is missing is one shared routing module so the policy survives the next contributor and the next model generation.

items.requirement: Hard, mechanically-enforced guardrails covering the codebase
items.evidence: [VERIFIED and strengthened.] Counted programmatically from package.json: `ci:gates` chains 125 `npm run` steps; 180 total `ci:*` scripts defined. scripts/gates-wired-baseline.json `files: []` — the meta-gate reports zero orphaned check-*.mjs today. Enforcement is in TWO independent places the auditor did not name: .github/workflows/ci.yml:45 `- run: npm run ci:gates` (plus :34 npm ci, :35 lint, :46 test, :51 build, :59 bundle-budget, :72 lighthouse, :82 a11y), and .husky/pre-push, which I read in full — it verifies a `rr-gates-marker` file whose tree hash must match the pushed tree, stamped by scripts/push-with-gates.sh after running ci:gates + eslint + build in a detached verify worktree. G45 producer-freeze confirmed: scripts/check-producer-freeze.mjs exists and 'producer-freeze' is present in the ci:gates string.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor flagged a stale '7 orphans' prose claim vs the empty baseline — that drift is real, but it missed two live weaknesses in the enforcement path.] (1) The pre-push hook is bypassable by design: `SKIP_LOCAL_GATES=1` short-circuits it, and the marker is accepted for up to `GATES_MARKER_MAX_AGE_MIN` (default 240 minutes), so a 4-hour-old green run can wave through a tree that changed since. CI in ci.yml is the real backstop. (2) The hook's own comments document three separate 2026-07-17 incidents where gates blocked clean pushes on foreign uncommitted state — i.e. the gate chain has itself been a reliability problem in a shared working tree.
items.why_it_matters: Strongest-built part of the domain and genuinely double-enforced. The bypass and marker-staleness window are the only holes, and both are documented in-hook rather than gated.

items.requirement: A cross-cutting audit capability that surfaces broken loops, stuck rows, dead crons, drifted skills — and actually runs
items.evidence: [VERIFIED] .claude/skills/deep-audit/SKILL.md exists with the 10-pass protocol and declares output at `out/audits/`. Re-checked on disk: `ls out/audits` => No such file or directory, while out/ itself contains 40+ sibling directories (admin-audit, admin-consolidation-review, admin-full-scan.txt, blog-posts, …), proving out/ is not gitignored-away or empty — deep-audit's specific path has simply never been written. docs/DEVELOPMENT_PROCESS.md line 40 designates `out/audits/` as the immune system's state ledger, so the canon points at a directory that does not exist.
items.gap: [VERIFIED, and it is a canon-level defect not just a skill-level one.] The immune-system row of the locked topology table names a state ledger that has never been created. Whatever cross-cutting auditing has happened (the `refactor(audit): #N` commit series in the last 14 days is clearly the product of a real audit) landed under other out/ paths and other doc names, so the canon cannot find its own audit history.
items.why_it_matters: The skill designed to catch everything else going stale writes to a path nothing reads and that does not exist — a self-referential instance of the exact failure it exists to catch.

items.requirement: The deterministic substrate (always-on machinery) actually running in production
items.evidence: [VERIFIED by parsing vercel.json myself — exactly 49 cron entries.] Spine coverage confirmed: sync-delta (4x/hr), sync-full, refresh-market-stats, refresh-mvs, 9 crm-* crons (auto-enroll, sequence-engine, gmail-sync, health-check, portal-lead-intake, scheduled-sends, bulk-worker, task-reminders, market-report-send), the full brain chain (producer-dispatcher `0 * * * *`, producer-runtime `0 * * * *`, publisher-sweep `*/30 * * * *`, marketing-measurement-loop `0 15 * * *`, marketing-weekly-cycle `0 16 * * 1`, marketing-audit-run `0 11 * * 2`), cma-build-worker `14,44 * * * *`, deploy-health `7,37 * * * *`. app/api/cron/loop-health-check/route.ts read in full — registered at `30 12 * * *`, cron-auth gated via requireCronAuth (line 28), iterates 10 channels checking marketing_channel_daily freshness with green/yellow/red thresholds plus an explicit value-aware zero-volume probe (comment at line ~57: 'recency alone is a LIAR').
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Substrate-only. loop-health-check monitors the MARKETING brain's wires exclusively — it has zero awareness of the four domain loops, so nothing in these 49 crons would have noticed crm-e2e going 13 days idle or experience-rollout stalling for 6 weeks. This layer diagnoses and reports; it never prioritizes, ships, measures, or learns.
items.why_it_matters: Proof that a loop wired to a Vercel cron with a real library behind it runs forever. The exact pattern to replicate — and loop-health-check is the natural place to add domain-loop staleness checks.

items.requirement: Every loop-related cron that exists in code is actually registered and running
items.evidence: [VERIFIED — the auditor was right and I confirmed each link.] app/api/cron/optimization-loop/route.ts exists (header line 8: 'Writes structured findings to optimization_runs table'). `grep -c optimization-loop vercel.json` => 0. The write path is real: lib/data/sync/syncWrites.ts:1054-1060 (`insertOptimizationRun`, `.from('optimization_runs').insert(row)`). The read path is real: app/actions/optimization-runs.ts:19 `.from('optimization_runs')`. So a complete write->store->read->UI chain exists with the trigger amputated.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Dead code, dead table, dead admin surface. 48 of 49 registered crons are live; this one route plus its DAL writer plus its server action plus its admin page are permanently inert. Note this is not an isolated case in kind — it is the same class as `out/audits/` and the two unwired ledgers: build the machinery, document it as part of the loop, never connect the trigger.
items.why_it_matters: Three independent instances of the identical failure class (optimization-loop, out/audits, the two ledgers) means the class is the finding, not the instance. Per the canon's own step 4, the fix is a gate that fails when an app/api/cron/*/route.ts has no vercel.json entry.

items.requirement: A heartbeat / staleness alarm so an idle loop is distinguishable from a waiting one
items.evidence: [MISSED BY THE AUDITOR as a requirement — it appears only in its shared_primitives list, not as a scored item.] No `loop_run_log`, `loop_heartbeat`, or equivalent table exists in docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT.md. The only per-loop state artifacts are unversioned files on one Mac: tmp/crm-e2e-latest.json (13 days stale, and tmp/ is a scratch dir), .auto-memory/fb-ads-loop-state.json (41 days stale), and prose status tables inside docs/EXPERIENCE_SYSTEM.md. app/api/cron/loop-health-check/route.ts checks marketing_channel_daily freshness per channel but has no concept of a domain loop.
items.gap: Loop liveness is stored in files that are not in a database, not backed up, not queried by any cron, and in one case sit in tmp/. Silence from a loop is unobservable, so 'stalled 6 weeks' and 'correctly waiting on Matt' render identically. This is the mechanism that let every other staleness finding in this audit persist undetected.
items.why_it_matters: Without this, adding schedulers just moves the blind spot — a scheduled loop that errors out silently is exactly as invisible as an unscheduled one.

items.requirement: A policy constraint bearing on 'run continuously to improve all features' (producer-layer freeze)
items.evidence: [VERIFIED] scripts/check-producer-freeze.mjs exists on disk and 'producer-freeze' is present in package.json's ci:gates chain (checked programmatically, not from docs). CLAUDE.md's 'Producer-layer freeze' section documents the 2026-06-09 Matt directive, the ratcheted REGISTRY row count, and the unfreeze condition (10 real posts through approve->publish->measure yielding a decision-grade insight, then Matt's explicit lift). Regenerating the baseline requires Matt's approval cited in the commit message.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Not a defect — a deliberate boundary condition. Worth noting the freeze's stated unfreeze metric ('10 real posts through approve->publish->measure') depends on the measurement chain, and marketing-measurement-loop IS registered and real — so unlike the site ledgers, this particular measure step has a live code path. The freeze is therefore falsifiable on its own terms, which the two loop ledgers are not.
items.why_it_matters: Any 'make the loops always-on' plan must be scoped as orchestration/infra maintenance, not new producer growth, or it trips G45.

shared_primitives_needed: A `loop_runs` heartbeat table in Supabase (loop_name, started_at, finished_at, outcome, blocked_on, artifacts) plus a DAL module, written by every loop firing and read by a staleness check bolted onto the already-registered /api/cron/loop-health-check — this closes the blind spot that hid every other staleness finding in this audit, and it must land BEFORE the schedulers or a scheduled loop that errors is exactly as invisible as an unscheduled one.

A mechanical gate (`ci:cron-registered`) that fails when any app/api/cron/*/route.ts has no matching vercel.json entry. Three independent instances of the same failure class exist today (optimization-loop unregistered, out/audits never created, both loop ledgers unwired) — per the canon's own step 4, fix the class.

Real DAL writers for `site_improvement_ledger` and `process_escape_ledger` (lib/data/loop/*.ts) invoked from the ship path, not from a bespoke one-time scheduled task that disables itself after firing once (which is literally what happened on 2026-07-08).

Four scheduled-task entries (or Vercel-cron-backed equivalents) invoking growth-loop / crm-e2e / tc-builder / experience-rollout on their own declared cadences — the mechanism is proven live (fb-verification-watch and ryan-realty-morning-briefing both fired within the last hour). Wire scripts/crm-e2e-verify.mjs into a cron first; it is already runnable code and is currently referenced by nothing.

A domain-agnostic adversarial-audit harness ported from lib/cma/audit.ts — keep its three real properties (independent LLM pass with no shared prompt, deterministic verdict computed in code via computeAuditVerdict, and the bounded single-round self-repair + re-audit at lib/cma/build.ts:246-270) but replace the CMA-welded input types with a generic claim/evidence contract so any loop can call it.

One shared model-routing module replacing the 5+ hardcoded model constants (producer-runtime/route.ts:44, cma/audit.ts:24, audit-classifier.ts:45, inbox-parser.ts:26, crm-inbox.ts:448) with a task-class -> model map, plus a lint gate that fails a new raw model-id literal. The routing DISCIPLINE already exists in code — it just has no single home and no enforcement.
open_questions_for_owner: Do you want the four domain loops converted into scheduled cloud-agent tasks like fb-verification-watch? The bridge does not exist. But note the harder question underneath: 550 commits landed in the last 14 days while every loop state ledger sat stale, which says the work is happening OUTSIDE the loop protocols. Is the fix to schedule the loops, or to make the ledgers a byproduct of shipping so they cannot go stale while work continues?
When you said '19 domains of work,' what is the enumerated list? The locked topology names only 5 loops plus substrate plus immune system. I need your list to build the coverage checklist.

What idle threshold marks a loop broken vs correctly waiting on you? Today the signal lives in tmp/crm-e2e-latest.json and .auto-memory/*.json on one machine, so there is no signal at all. I would propose N days idle with open unblocked work, per-loop threshold your call.

Should `site_improvement_ledger` / `process_escape_ledger` be wired now? Worth knowing: the only write ever performed was by a one-off scheduled task on 2026-07-08 that disabled itself afterward, so the canon's prioritization `confidence` term has never had data behind it.
Does the G45 producer freeze cover building the orchestration/scheduling infra itself, or is that exempt as maintenance on the existing five loops?
